summary: Levocarnitine (L-carnitine) is a carrier molecule essential for mitochondrial fatty-acid metabolism, used to treat primary systemic carnitine deficiency and secondary carnitine deficiency from inborn errors of metabolism. Oral formulations are for oral use only (not parenteral); IV forms are used chiefly in end-stage renal disease on dialysis. It is generally well tolerated, with GI complaints and body odor that improve with slower intake or dose reduction, and rare hypersensitivity reactions.
indications: Treatment of primary systemic carnitine deficiency (presenting with Reye-like encephalopathy, hypoketotic hypoglycemia, and/or cardiomyopathy)

Acute and chronic treatment of secondary carnitine deficiency due to an inborn error of metabolism (e.g., glutaric aciduria II, methylmalonic aciduria, propionic acidemia, medium-chain acyl-CoA dehydrogenase deficiency)
IV formulations: carnitine deficiency in end-stage renal disease patients on dialysis

dosage.d: 1 to 3 g/day (10-30 mL oral solution) for a 50 kg subject; start at 1 g/day (10 mL/day) and titrate slowly
dosage.t: Spaced evenly throughout the day, every 3-4 hours, during or after meals
dosage.n: Higher doses only with caution where clinical/biochemical findings suggest benefit

dosage.d: 50 to 100 mg/kg/day (0.5 mL/kg/day oral solution); start at 50 mg/kg/day, titrate slowly to max 3 g/day (30 mL/day)
dosage.n: Adjust to tolerance and therapeutic response

dosage.c: Carnitine deficiency in ESRD on dialysis
dosage.d: IV levocarnitine per applicable IV product labeling
dosage.n: Oral solution is NOT for parenteral use; use an approved IV product

admin: Oral solution is for oral/internal use only - NOT for parenteral use
Consume slowly and space doses evenly throughout the day (every 3-4 hours), preferably during or after meals, to maximize tolerance
May be taken alone or dissolved in drink or other liquid food to reduce taste fatigue
Rapid consumption can cause GI reactions; greater dilution and slower intake help
Monitor tolerance closely during the first week and after any dose increase
moa: Levocarnitine is a naturally occurring substance required in mammalian energy metabolism. It facilitates entry of long-chain fatty acids into cellular mitochondria, delivering substrate for oxidation and subsequent energy production; fatty acids are the main energy substrate in skeletal and cardiac muscle. In carnitine deficiency, supplementation restores this transport. In disorders that accumulate toxic acyl-CoA compounds (organic acidemias), levocarnitine binds the acyl group to form acylcarnitine, which is readily excreted, thereby clearing the toxic compound and relieving the resulting acidosis.

absolute: None known per labeling (use caution with prior hypersensitivity)
relative: Severely compromised renal function or ESRD on dialysis with chronic high oral doses (risk of TMA/TMAO accumulation)
monitor: Periodic blood chemistries and vital signs

preg: Reproductive studies in rats and rabbits at doses up to 3.8 times the human dose (by surface area) revealed no evidence of impaired fertility or fetal harm. There are no adequate and well-controlled studies in pregnant women; because animal studies are not always predictive, use during pregnancy only if clearly needed.
lact: Levocarnitine supplementation in nursing mothers has not been specifically studied. Studies in dairy cows show milk carnitine concentration increases after administration. Weigh any risk to the infant from excess carnitine intake against the benefit of supplementation to the mother; consider discontinuing nursing or treatment.
renal: Safety and efficacy of oral levocarnitine have not been evaluated in renal insufficiency. Chronic high oral doses in patients with severely compromised renal function or in ESRD patients on dialysis may cause accumulation of the potentially toxic metabolites trimethylamine (TMA) and trimethylamine-N-oxide (TMAO), normally excreted in urine. IV levocarnitine is the form used in dialysis-associated deficiency.
hepatic: No specific hepatic dosage adjustment is provided in the labeling.

moderate: Warfarin - reports of increased INR; monitor INR after starting levocarnitine or after dose adjustments
interactions.food: May be consumed alone or dissolved in drink/liquid food; take during or after meals and slowly to improve tolerance.

serious: Seizures (in patients with or without pre-existing seizure activity; may increase frequency/severity)
rare: Mild myasthenia (described in uremic patients receiving D,L-carnitine)
emergency: Anaphylaxis, laryngeal edema, bronchospasm (reported with IV use, mostly in ESRD dialysis patients)

monitoring: Periodic blood chemistries and vital signs
Overall clinical condition and GI tolerance, especially in the first week and after dose increases
counsel: Take doses slowly and spread them through the day, with or after meals, to reduce stomach upset
Oral solution is for swallowing only - never inject it
Reducing the dose often lessens body odor or GI symptoms
Seek medical attention for rash, hives, facial swelling, or trouble breathing
Tell your clinician if you take warfarin (blood thinner) so clotting tests can be checked
pk: Not specifically defined; corrects deficiency over days of dosing
Tmax ~3.3 h (Cmax ~80 micromol/L after oral dosing); serum max 2-4.5 h
Apparent terminal ~17.4 h after IV (distribution half-life ~0.585 h)
Maintained with evenly spaced multiple daily dosing
Store at controlled room temperature 15-30 C (59-86 F)
pearls: Oral solution is NOT for parenteral use - use an approved IV product when the IV route is needed
Absolute oral bioavailability is low (~15%); space doses every 3-4 hours with meals
Body odor and GI upset are dose-related and usually improve with dose reduction or greater dilution
Monitor INR in patients on warfarin after initiation or dose change
In ESRD/dialysis, chronic high oral doses risk TMA/TMAO accumulation; levocarnitine is readily removed by dialysis
missed: Take the missed dose when remembered, then resume the usual evenly spaced schedule; do not double up. Consistent daily intake supports steady carnitine levels.
overdose: No reports of toxicity from overdosage. Levocarnitine is easily removed from plasma by dialysis. Large doses may cause diarrhea. Manage with supportive care.
